newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian deputy PM warns Duma over economic reforms. [CORRECTED 12:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Russian deputy PM warns Duma over economic reforms. [CORRECTED 12:50 GMT]

text.p: Oleg Sysuyev (corrects from "Sysuev"), one of the top reformers in the Russian government, warned the opposition-dominated parliament on Wednesday that ministers' patience was wearing thin over deputies' resistance to economic reforms.

Sysuyev (corrects from "Sysuev") told a news conference he personally did not favour dissolution of the State Duma lower chamber but the executive branch could raise the issue "in a tough manner" later this year. Only President Boris Yeltsin has the right to call an early election.

"The Duma is doing all it can to create an extraordinarily tense situation by the autumn, to force the president to change policy. This will not happen," said Sysuyev, whose package of bills cutting welfare benefits was rejected by the Duma on Tuesday.

"The question of changing the Duma may be raised by the executive branch. It may raise it in a tough manner," he said adding that he personally favoured carrying on his "difficult and sometimes repugnant work" with the current chamber.

First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais on Tuesday accused the Duma of being "incapable of working" after it rose for its summer recess having rejected two of three key pieces of economic reform legislation. He said the question of dissolution was up to Yeltsin.

Asked about Chubais's remarks, Yeltsin's spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Wednesday morning: "Despite the Duma's frequent refusal to work with the executive and hide under cover of populism, the executive is inclined to cooperate with the Duma, as it considers this essential for the country."
